subject: cell indices and subset option for plotDensity

messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: cell indices and subset option for plotDensity
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to call plotDensity for a subset of probes. I thought I
could give indices, as from the result of calling getCellIndices(), but
this is not working. This is giving me indices beyond the allowed range
and now I think I'm completely incorrect about what getCellIndices()
returns.

Basically I have a cdf (cdfHjay) that contains all my probes and a
subset cdf (cdfHjayJuc) that contains, well, a subset. What I want to do is

psrCells<-getCellIndices(cdfHjayPsr)
plotDensity(csBRCAJunct,col="black",lwd=2)
plotDensity(csBRCAJunct,subset=unlist(psrCells),col="red",lwd=2,add=TRUE)

the idea being to compare the density of the intensity. I thought this
should work, but I get the following error:

> plotDensity(csBRCAJunct,subset=unlist(psrCells),col="red",lwd=2,add=TRUE)
Error in list("plotDensity(csBRCAJunct, subset = unlist(psrCells), col =
"red", lwd = 2, a" = <environment>, :

[2008-08-13 14:49:15] Exception: Range of argument 'indices' is out of
range [1,6553600]: [2569,6556156]

[%s,%s]", .n

disallow)

invokeRestart("muffleWarnin

lwd = 2, a
Calls: plotDensity -> plotDensity.AffymetrixCelSet
Execution halted

It seems that my cell indices are beyond the limits. These are highly
questionable cdfs, so I did some spot checking. My array is 2560x2560.
So I've taken a couple of probesets that are in both cdfs to check that
they have the same x,y coordinates (and that they are <=2560)and they
seem fine:

> readUnits(cdfHjayJuc,units=unitsJuc)[[1]]$groups[[1]][c("x","y")]
$x
[1] 2257 1400 1537 1400 679 1536 222 1536

$y
[1] 2394 2560 2454 735 296 1570 1438 1822

> readUnits(cdfHjay,units=unitsAll)[[1]]$groups[[1]][c("x","y")]
$x
[1] 2257 1400 1537 1400 679 1536 222 1536

$y
[1] 2394 2560 2454 735 296 1570 1438 1822

I thought the index was x*y, but this is not what getCellIndices returns
(which is why I got an error -- some of these values are beyond 2560^2).
> getCellIndices(cdfHjayJuc,units=unitsJuc)[[1]]
$groups
$groups$JUC0100002335_st
$groups$JUC0100002335_st$indices
[1] 6130898 6555001 6283778 1883001 758440 4020737 3681503 4665857
> getCellIndices(cdfHjay,units=unitsAll)[[1]]
$groups
$groups$JUC0100002335_st
$groups$JUC0100002335_st$indices
[1] 6130898 6555001 6283778 1883001 758440 4020737 3681503 4665857

So my questions are
1) what does getCellIndices return?
2) what do I pass to 'subset' in plotDensity that will do what I want?

Thanks,
Elizabeth

> ( why is 1 added? )

'x' and 'y' are indexed starting from zero whereas cell indices are
indexed starting from one. The former is specified by the file format
and the Fusion SDK (used by affxparser and hence aroma.affymetrix),
whereas the latter is calculated by 'affxparser' and there we decided
to start from one because it is much more natural when working with R.

For more details, see for instance help("2. Cell coordinates and cell
indices") of 'affxparser'.

So, in your case 'x' and 'y' are in [0,2559], and 'indices' is in [1,2560*2560].

Is it possible that you missed that (x,y) should start from zero? For
instance, the maximum cell index reported in Elizabeth's error message
is "6556156". If you subtract "one row", that is 2560, you get
6553596, which equals 2560^2-4, i.e. within the range.

Hope this helps

Henrik

parts:
By the way, Henrik, the help file has i=2600000, but it should be
i=2560000 for the equations given there.

Also, I'm not clear on what you mean by mod(i-1,K) in the help -- I
think you mean mean integer division and not modulo? Suppose K=N=100 and
x=0, y=20 => i=2001. Then (i-1) mod K = 0 but |_(i-1)/K_|=20 (difference
between %% and %/% in terms of R commands).

Best, Elizabeth

parts: Hi,

On Thu, Aug 14, 2008 at 3:16 PM, Elizabeth Purdom <epu...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> By the way, Henrik, the help file has i=2600000, but it should be
> i=2560000 for the equations given there.
Correct. Typo.

>
> Also, I'm not clear on what you mean by mod(i-1,K) in the help -- I
> think you mean mean integer division and not modulo? Suppose K=N=100 and
> x=0, y=20 => i=2001. Then (i-1) mod K = 0 but |_(i-1)/K_|=20 (difference
> between %% and %/% in terms of R commands).

Your right, it should be integer division, not modulo (that error
probably originates from an earlier version where x was first
calculated by using modulo and the y).

I've now updated it to read floor((i-1)/K). (I avoid using '%' in Rd
help files because they have to be escaped etc).

All of the above has been fixed for the next release of affxparser.

Thanks for spotting this.

Henrik

> Best, Elizabeth
